description: Single-DGX-Spark dense Qwen3.8-27B (Gated DeltaNet plus full attention) on the creator's TensorFold fork (taussoe/TensorFold branch glm-long-context at c32abe92: TensorFold 0.3.6.3 plus the creator's long-context work; exact decoding: drafted replies equal serial ones; custom CUDA kernels JIT-compiled on first start) with Vontra's MLX 4-bit checkpoint and z-lab's DFlash2 draft model proposing token trees of 12 rows, following taussoe's tensorfold-recipes (d8a7c09c, MIT, NODES=1), which builds that fork branch on a Spark by default (TENSORFOLD_SOURCE=local; the base follows that declaration). Text only. Upstream measured on one Spark (TensorFold 0.3.6.1): decode 59 / 52 / 56 / 52 tok/s in the standard cells (code and chat, sampled and greedy), code as a chat reply 96 / 111, a 32k prompt read at 1,579 tok/s; serial decoding without the draft model is 13.1 tok/s, so drafting is where the speed comes from (upstream figures, unmeasured here). TensorFold's published concurrency figure on one Spark is 161.7 tok/s at 16 streams in flight (25.4 GiB peak, context 8192; TensorFold's own benchmark). The memory envelope is TensorFold's startup estimate of 62.5 GiB at the 262,144-token window for the sibling NVFP4 checkpoint; upstream states none for this checkpoint. Both the checkpoint and the draft model are Apache-2.0 (the DFlash2 draft model per its card). The fork is older than the TensorFold 0.6.0 this recipe carried before (no xgrammar structured-output support, which arrived in 0.6.0); the recipe keeps every option it passes. Thinking is chosen per request (chat template kwargs or sampling parameters), not as a recipe option; server default: Open a think block by default (TensorFold default).
title: Qwen3.8 27B TensorFold single Spark (taussoe)
